source: NCERT Class IX, India and the Contemporary World I, History Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Nomadic Pastoralists
points: **Pastoralists** = communities that rear **animals (cattle, sheep, goats, camels)** and move seasonally in search of **pasture and water** — a way of life called **nomadic pastoralism**.
Movement follows the seasons — up to mountains in summer, down to plains in winter (**transhumance**).

sections.heading: 2. Pastoral Communities of India
points: **Gujjar Bakarwals** (Jammu & Kashmir) — herd goats and sheep.
**Gaddi shepherds** (Himachal Pradesh).
**Dhangars** (Maharashtra) — shepherds/blanket weavers.
**Gollas, Kurumas, Kurubas** (south India); **Banjaras** (many states); **Raikas** (Rajasthan, camel and cattle herders).
They move with the seasons between mountains, plains and dry regions.

sections.heading: 3. Colonial Impact on Pastoralists
points: Colonial laws squeezed pastoralists:

sub: **Waste Land Rules** — 'uncultivated' grazing land taken over and given for cultivation.
**Forest Acts** — grazing restricted in reserved/protected forests.
**Criminal Tribes Act (1871)** — branded many nomadic communities as 'criminal', restricting their movement.
**Grazing Tax** — pastoralists taxed for every animal grazed.

points: As pastures shrank, pastoralists suffered — some reduced herds, some settled, some found new routes.

sections.heading: 4. Pastoralists in Africa — the Maasai
points: The **Maasai** of **East Africa (Kenya, Tanzania)** were cattle herders.
Colonial rule took their best grazing land for **white settlers and game reserves (e.g. Serengeti, Maasai Mara)**; borders confined them.
Their pastures shrank, causing hardship, drought deaths and social change (elders vs warriors).
Like Indian pastoralists, they **adapted** to survive.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Pastoralists rear animals & move seasonally (transhumance) for pasture/water.
India: Gujjar Bakarwals (J&K), Gaddis (HP), Dhangars (Maharashtra), Raikas (Rajasthan, camels).
Colonial squeeze: Waste Land Rules, Forest Acts, Criminal Tribes Act (1871), Grazing Tax.
Africa: Maasai (Kenya/Tanzania) lost land to settlers & game reserves.
Pastoralists adapted (reduced herds, new routes, part settlement).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Criminal Tribes Act (1871)** wrongly branded many nomads as 'criminal'.
**Waste Land Rules** took grazing land for cultivation, hurting pastoralists.
The **Maasai** are East African (Kenya/Tanzania) cattle herders.
**Transhumance** = seasonal movement between highland and lowland pastures.
